clue.text: Trophy and badge for sex god

parts.note: a cup is a trophy awarded to a winner
ID, identification, is a badge or card showing who you are

explanation.surface: An award and a badge handed out to the god of love himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of erotic love, son of Venus, is often drawn with bow and arrows.

clue.text: Short tennis player once starting to serve in the net?

parts.note: Pat Cash, the Australian who won Wimbledon in 1987

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is all that is wanted here

parts.note: caught in a net is trapped

explanation.surface: A short former tennis player begins serving into the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of the player's height; it is the definition, meaning lacking money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of funds is an informal synonym for having very little money to spend.

clue.text: Early on, rug's clean around the edge

indicators.note: the word for clean sits round the outside, its edge enclosing the rest

parts.note: pure means clean, unsullied
re means on, concerning
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: Starting early on the clean-up of a rug's border.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening before its proper time is early, the adjective as in a too-soon birth.

clue.text: Idiots play sport on Sunday

parts.note: to do a play or part is to perform it
PE, physical education, is school sport

explanation.surface: Fools who insist on playing games on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is slang for a stupid person, a fool or nitwit.

clue.text: Damage flesh with knife?

indicators.note: damaged flesh is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a knife is an arm in the sense of a weapon

explanation.surface: Cutting one's own skin with a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damage' rearranges FLESH into SELFH; a knife is an example of an arm, a weapon, hence the question mark. The whole clue also describes the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately injuring one's own body, for instance by cutting, is what the phrase describes.

clue.text: They watch as three points can go to Golf driver

parts.note: S, E and N are three points of the compass
a tin is a can
Ernie Els, the South African golfer, who drives the ball

explanation.surface: A golfer is promised three points for a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentries or guards keep watch, so they are those who watch.

clue.text: Top escort

definitions.meaning: first place, in front of all others
to guide or conduct someone along

explanation.definitionFit: Being in first position, and guiding someone along, are both senses of the word.

clue.text: House carpet needing constant ____?

indicators.note: needing is used as lacking, so the letter for constant is missing

parts.note: a carpet is a floor covering
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A house whose carpet needs vacuuming all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is the answer, filling in the sentence; 'needing' means lacking, so C goes from COVERING, leaving OVERING.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet in a busy house needs constant vacuuming, Hoover being the brand name used as a verb in Britain.

clue.text: Johnny stripped after right piece of music

indicators.note: the stripped word comes after the letter for right
stripped means its outer letters are taken off

parts.note: British slang for a condom

explanation.surface: A man called Johnny undresses after some music is played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Johnny' is British slang for a condom; stripped of its outer letters it gives ONDO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form with a recurring theme, often a movement of a sonata.

clue.text: A nude girl's open about being promiscuous

indicators.note: about means turned around, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naked girl is frank about her many partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Having many casual sexual partners is the informal phrase's meaning.

clue.text: Hotel on old TV show half-heartedly served up this?

definitions.text: Hotel on old TV show half-heartedly served up this?

parts.note: the Waldorf, a famous New York hotel

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means written upwards, read backwards
half the heart is lost: one of the two central L letters goes

parts.note: Dallas, the US soap of the 1970s and 80s

explanation.surface: A hotel in an old sitcom serves up this dish without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: The dish was born at the Waldorf hotel, and 'Waldorf Salad' is a Fawlty Towers episode, the classic British hotel sitcom, which is why the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad of apple, celery and walnuts in mayonnaise, created at the Waldorf hotel and title of a Fawlty Towers episode.

clue.text: Fur coat and no knickers, primarily? Lass that is false

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters are rearranged
primarily means only the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: The phrase 'fur coat and no knickers', all show and no substance, applied to a fake lass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fur coat and no knickers' is a British put-down for someone showy but common underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal's pelt is made into coats, so the fur is a coat's material.

clue.text: Felt item of clothing; a piece turned over to iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: turned over means the words are read backwards

parts.note: rod is slang for a gun, a piece

explanation.surface: Pressing a garment of felt: a piece is turned for ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft brimmed hat usually made of felt, an item worn on the head.

clue.text: When excited, hug or kiss thug

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so they are rearranged

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: A thug gets excited by a hug or a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, uncouth or violent man is a synonym for a thug.

clue.text: Car to sit on tail

parts.note: a bird sits on eggs to hatch them
a tail is the back of something

explanation.surface: A car sitting right on your tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sit on tail' reads as tailgating; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A car body type with a rear door opening upwards, hence an example of a car.

clue.text: Tired one in 10 can kip over

indicators.note: over means turned over, the pieces read backwards

parts.note: Bo Derek, the star of the 1979 film 10
K is the abbreviation for the kip, the currency of Laos

explanation.surface: Someone tired out who can nap at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kip' looks like British slang for a nap; it is the money of Laos. '10' is the film starring Bo Derek.
explanation.definitionFit: Knackered is British slang for utterly exhausted.

clue.text: I have sex with male inside lodge

indicators.note: inside means the letter for male goes within the other pieces

parts.note: to bed someone is to have sex with them

explanation.surface: A man boasts of a romp with a man in a lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as I + BED with the letter for male inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something firmly in a surrounding mass is to lodge it, the variant spelling of embed.

clue.text: British motor has crashed where Americans go

indicators.note: a crashed motor is wrecked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British car has crashed where Americans drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans say they are going to the bathroom when they mean the toilet, a euphemism.

clue.text: Fold two pages, time to finish second one

indicators.note: the letter for time goes at the end of the second page word, replacing its last letter

parts.note: P is a page, and a leaf is a second page

explanation.surface: Folding two pages, then finishing the second one.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pages are P and LEAF; T replaces the final F of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold pressed into cloth.

clue.text: Clobber that's horrible, one criticising clothing

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around the other piece

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly, so one who does so is a slater
ugh is the cry meaning that's horrible

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses some clothes as horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like British slang for clothes; it is the verb, to defeat heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To clobber an opponent is to beat them heavily, a rout or massacre.

clue.text: Blue Planet back on telly

parts.note: the Earth is a planet

indicators.note: the back of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: The nature series Blue Planet returns to the television.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue Planet is a BBC nature documentary series.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue humour is crude or bawdy, as is earthy humour.

clue.text: Recipe in back reviewed and not cooked so well

indicators.note: in places the letter for recipe inside the other word
reviewed in this sense means viewed in reverse, read backwards

parts.note: the rear is the back
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A recipe in the back pages is reviewed as undercooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that is rare is barely cooked; a comparative for less well done.

clue.text: Former cycling team used to be holding road up

parts.note: Team Sky, the British cycling team, now renamed

indicators.note: holding means containing, wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: was means used to be

explanation.surface: A former cycling team once held the road climbing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Towards the sky is upwards, an adverb of direction.

clue.text: Puppy beginning to walk further

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: to further a cause is to help it

explanation.surface: A puppy begins to walk further.
explanation.definitionFit: A whelp is a young dog, a pup.

clue.text: Conservative getting in money counter

parts.note: in means fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: A Tory joins a money-counting job.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling chip is a token standing for money, a counter.

clue.text: Flying down, missing nothing? Large hooter

definitions.text: Flying down, missing nothing? Large hooter

indicators.note: flying letters are scattered about, so they are rearranged
missing means the letter for nothing is dropped

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A big owl swooping down, missing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes O out of DOWN to give DWN, which is jumbled with LARGE HOOTER. A hooter is an owl, and the big horned owl misses nothing as it flies down.
explanation.definitionFit: A large American owl with ear tufts like horns, a large hooting bird of prey.

clue.text: One gets worn down when stopping in talked about holiday accommodation

definitions.text: One gets worn down when stopping

indicators.note: talked about means spoken, so the word is as it sounds

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
a pad is slang for a place to live

explanation.surface: Discussing the holiday flat while stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: The friction block in a car's braking system wears down each time it is used.

clue.text: Sat second exam primarily in school

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for school

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Sitting a second exam at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat' suggests sitting an exam; it means sat for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose is to sit for a painter, so posed and sat are synonyms.
